steps.text: Make the US$250 first deposit using any of the listed payment methods.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Adjust the risk controls, pick a mode and practise on the demo before going live.

pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
cons: Registration details not stated up front.
The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
Performance examples without dates or proof.
Asset list that shifts between pages.
redFlags: Restriction lists that name different countries.
Payout promises with no processing detail.
No regulator, licence or audit named anywhere.

faqs.a: Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

faqs.q: Where is Kong Global Trade restricted?
faqs.a: The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

bottomLine: For a cautious newcomer, Kong Global Trade can work: start on the demo, deposit the US$250 minimum and keep your own numbers.
The verdict holds at 4.5: research it, demo it, and if you fund it, fund the minimum. The platform earns a careful start, not blind trust.
